CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  2175 Cherry Avenue • Signal Hill, California 90755-3799

  THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  WELCOMES YOU TO A REGULAR
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  December 12, 2023

The City of Signal Hill appreciates your attendance. Citizen interest provides the Council and
Agency with valuable information regarding issues of the community. Meetings are held on
the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of every month.

Meetings begin at 6:00 pm with the conduct of any business permitted to be conducted in
closed session by the Brown Act (Government Code Section 54950, et seq.), if any, and with
the public portion of the meeting beginning at 7:00 pm. There is a period for public comment
on closed session matters at 6:00 pm prior to the closed session. In the event there is no
business to be conducted in closed session, the regular meeting shall begin at 7:00 pm.
There is a public comment period at the beginning of the regular meeting. Any person
wishing to comment shall be allotted three minutes per distinct item. Any meeting may be
adjourned to a time and place stated in the order of adjournment.

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting on the City’s website and outside of City
Hall. The agenda and related reports are also available for review online at
www.cityofsignalhill.org.

To view the meeting live at 6:00 p.m.:

  • City of Signal Hill website at www.cityofsignalhill.org, select the City Council
  Meetings Link from the home page.
To participate during the regular City Council meeting at 6:00 p.m.:

  • In-person Participation: Council Chamber of City Hall, 2175 Cherry Avenue, Signal
  Hill, California.
  • To make a general public comment or comment on a specific agenda item, you may
  also submit your comment, limited to 250 words or less, to the City Clerk at
  cityclerk@cityofsignalhill.org not later than 4:00 p.m. on Tuesday, December 12, 2023.
  Written comments will be provided electronically to City Council and attached to the
  meeting minutes. Written comments will not be read into the record.
City Council Members are compensated $722.18 per month. City Clerk and City Treasurer are

  Page 1 of 10
 City Council  Regular  December 12, 2023

compensated $438.22 per month.

(1)  CALL TO ORDER – 6:00 P.M.

(2)  ROLL CALL

  MAYOR HANSEN
  VICE MAYOR WOODS
  COUNCIL MEMBER COPELAND
  COUNCIL MEMBER JONES
  COUNCIL MEMBER WILSON
(3)  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

(4)  PUBLIC BUSINESS FROM THE FLOOR ON ITEMS NOT LISTED ON THE AGENDA
  (SPEAKERS WILL BE GIVEN THREE MINUTES FOR EACH DISTINCT ITEM)

(5)  COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENTS

(6)  CITY MANAGER REPORTS

  a.  CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  Summary:

  The City Council will reorganize by selecting a new Mayor and Vice Mayor.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness of City services.
  Recommendations:

  1. The City Council will reorganize by selecting a new Mayor and Vice Mayor.
  2. The newly appointed Mayor will present a proclamation to outgoing Mayor
  Hansen.
  b.  PROFESSIONAL CONSULTANT SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH DUDEK TO
  PREPARE AN UPDATE TO THE WATER MASTER PLAN AND RATE STUDY

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider approving a Professional Consultant Services
  Agreement with Dudek for the preparation of an update to the 2018 Water
  Master Plan (WMP) and the 2019 Water System Rate Study, in the amount of
  $336,423 (with a contingency of up to $33,642.30). The City released a Request
  for Proposals (RFP) for these services on November 3, 2023, with a proposal
  due date of November 27, 2023; the City received two proposals by the
  deadline. Following staff review of proposals and interviews, Dudek was the

  Page 2 of 10
 City Council  Regular  December 12, 2023

  highest ranked firm. Based on the evaluation process, staff believes Dudek is
  the best qualified firm with the proper experience to prepare a comprehensive
  water master plan based on the qualification criteria identified in the RFP. If
  approved by the City Council, staff anticipates work can begin on December 15,
  2023, and be completed within a nine-month period, by fall 2024, from the
  contract start date.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s  physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendations:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to enter into a Professional Consultant Services
  Agreement with Dudek for the preparation of an update to the 2018 Water
  Master Plan and 2019 Rate Study, for a 9-month term contract (with one 3
  -month extension) for a not-to-exceed contract amount of $336,423, in a
  form approved by the City Attorney.

  2. Authorize the Public Works Director to utilize a project contingency of up to
  10% ($33,642.30).

  3. Adopt a resolution entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA AMENDING THE ADOPTED BUDGET AND AUTHORIZING
  BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-24
  c.  ANNUAL COMPREHENSIVE FINANCIAL REPORT FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2022-23

  Summary:

  The Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) is an independently
  audited summary report of the financial transactions of the City for Fiscal Year
  (FY) 2022-23, providing relevant financial information to the City Council,
  residents, current and future employees, grant entities, creditors, bond investors,
  rating agencies, and other interested parties. This audit is performed in
  compliance with City Charter requirements with the results presented to the City
  Council for review.

  The audit was completed by the City's independent auditor, RAMS, Rogers,
  Anderson, Malody & Scott, LLP, Certified Public Accountants, which issued an
  unqualified opinion audit report, otherwise known as a “clean opinion” finding
  nothing of material concern in the City’s internal controls, financial, and
  bookkeeping practices. The independent auditor’s unmodified report provides
  assurance the ACFR, and the audited information within, present fairly the City’s
  financial position for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2023.

  Page 3 of 10
 City Council  Regular  December 12, 2023

  As part of this report, staff normally provides detailed information and allocation
  recommendations regarding any General Fund Operating Surplus or Deficit.
  The FY 2022-23 General Fund surplus is $8.0 million as reported in the ACFR.
  Staff will return to the City Council on January 23, 2024, to provide
  recommendations regarding the proposed surplus appropriations.  This
  proposed time extension will allow staff to conduct a detailed analysis of the
  surplus that will identify ongoing revenue updates, requests to re-appropriate
  unutilized budget appropriations, one-time expenditure requests for department
  operations, programs or special projects, and reserve allocations resulting in
  budget adjustments for the current fiscal year.
  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability and
  resilience.

  Recommendations:

  1. Receive and file the City’s ACFR for FY 2022-23.

  2. Direct staff to return in January with proposed appropriations for the FY 2022
  -23 General Fund operating surplus.

  3. Direct staff to distribute copies of the ACFR for FY 2022-23 as required, as
  well as to the Office of the City Clerk to be placed on file for the general
  public and posted on the City’s website.
  d.  2024 COMMEMORATIVE FLAG DISPLAY SCHEDULE

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider adopting the 2024 Commemorative Flag Display
  Schedule by resolution.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning  Government:  Strengthen  internal
  communication, recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to
  increase the effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendation:

  Adopt the resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING THE 2024 COMMEMORATIVE FLAG DISPLAY
  SCHEDULE

  Page 4 of 10
 City Council  Regular  December 12, 2023

(7)  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following Consent Calendar items are expected to be routine and
  non-controversial. Items will be acted upon by the Council at one time without
  discussion. Any item may be removed by a Council Member for discussion.
  a.  WAIVE THE READING OF ORDINANCES IN FULL AND AUTHORIZE
  READING BY TITLE ONLY

  Summary:

  The recommended action waives reading of ordinances in full and authorizes
  reading by title only. The purpose of this item is to help streamline the Council
  meeting process, to avoid unnecessary delay and to allow more time for
  substantive discussion of items on the agenda.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendation:

  Waive the reading of all ordinances. Wherein the titles appear on the public
  agenda; said titles shall be determined to have been read by title, and further
  reading is waived.
  b.  ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 2023-11-1545 ADDING CHAPTERS 5.06
  (SIDEWALK VENDING), 5.36 (MOBILE FOOD VENDING), 8.58 (VACANT
  PROPERTY MAINTENANCE), 9.65 (MEDIAN ISLANDS), 9.66 (CATALYTIC
  CONVERTERS), AND 9.67 (SPEED CONTESTS); AMENDING CHAPTERS
  5.14 (FILMING ACTIVITIES), 8.13 (ADMINISTRATIVE CITATION), 9.08
  (CONDUCT IN PUBLIC PLACES), 9.18 (LOUD OR UNRULY PARTIES,
  GATHERINGS AND OTHER DISTURBANCES OF THE PEACE), 1.01 (CODE
  ADOPTION), 12.14 (CAMPING AND STORAGE OF PERSONAL PROPERTY
  ON  PUBLIC  PROPERTY),  1.14 (MUNICIPAL  ELECTION),  2.04
  (ADMINISTRATIVE  OFFICER),  2.08 (COUNCIL  MEETINGS),  2.80
  (PERSONNEL RULES FOR CLASSIFIED AND NON-CLASSIFIED
  EMPLOYEES), OF THE SIGNAL HILL MUNICIPAL CODE TO IMPROVE AND
  ENHANCE OPERATION OF THE CITY; AND FINDING THE ORDINANCE AS
  EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT

  Summary:

  In a proactive initiative to modernize the Signal Hill (“City”) Municipal Code, City
  staff and the City Attorney’s office have worked together to identify portions of
  the City’s Municipal Code requiring updates to conform with State law and
  integrate best practices. This collaborative effort has resulted in amendments
  and new additions to the City’s Municipal Code including, but not limited to, code
  Page 5 of 10
 City Council  Regular  December 12, 2023

  enforcement, vending regulations, health and safety, and other updates tailored
  to fit the community’s evolving needs. These updates to the Municipal Code are
  presented to the City Council in one comprehensive omnibus ordinance.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 2  Community Safety: Maintain Community Safety by supporting
  public safety services and increasing emergency preparedness.

  Goal No. 3  Economic & Downtown Development: Improve the local economy,
  support local businesses, and create a vibrant downtown core.

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s  physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention systems, and processes to increase
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendation:

  Adopt Ordinance No. 2023-11-1545, entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL Hill,
  CALIFORNIA, ADDING CHAPTER 5.06 (SIDEWALK VENDING), 5.36 (MOBILE
  FOOD VENDING), 8.58 (VACANT PROPERTY MAINTENANCE), 9.65
  (MEDIAN ISLANDS), 9.66 (CATALYTIC CONVERTERS), AND 9.67 (SPEED
  CONTESTS); AMENDING CHAPTERS 5.14 (FILMING ACTIVITIES), 8.13
  (ADMINISTRATIVE CITATION), 9.08 (CONDUCT IN PUBLIC PLACES), 9.18
  (LOUD OR UNRULY PARTIES, GATHERINGS AND OTHER DISTURBANCES
  OF THE PEACE), 1.01 (CODE ADOPTION), 12.14 (CAMPING AND STORAGE
  OF PERSONAL PROPERTY ON PUBLIC PROPERTY), 1.14 (MUNICIPAL
  ELECTION), 2.04 (ADMINISTRATIVE OFFICER), 2.08 (COUNCIL MEETINGS),
  2.80 (PERSONNEL RULES FOR CLASSIFIED AND NON-CLASSIFIED
  EMPLOYEES), AND 21.28 (TIME OF PAYMENT AND FINANCIAL
  CONTROLS) OF THE SIGNAL HILL MUNICIPAL CODE TO IMPROVE AND
  ENHANCE OPERATION OF THE CITY; AND FINDING THE ORDINANCE AS
  EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT
  c.  CONTRACT SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH ANDREW (AJ) DAVIS OF
  PROJECT STREET GOLD FOR THE DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, AND
  INSTALLATION OF OUTDOOR PUBLIC ART IN THE SIGNAL HILL PUBLIC
  LIBRARY ZINNIA COURTYARD

  Summary:

  The City has a history of incorporating art into parks and public facilities. With
  the opening of the Signal Hill Public Library, the City Council desired to enhance
  the Signal Hill Public Library Zinnia Courtyard by encouraging creative

  Page 6 of 10
 City Council  Regular  December 12, 2023

  expression. To effectuate this purpose, the City Council formed the Arts
  Sub-Committee (subcommittee) to facilitate the process and approved issuance
  of a Request for Proposals (RFP) for an outdoor public art project.

  The City released the RFP in June 2023 and received 21 proposals.
  Subsequently, one artist withdrew their proposal leaving a total of 20 proposals.
  Following review of proposals, the subcommittee selected five (5) artists for an
  interview. Upon conclusion of the evaluation process, the subcommittee
  recommends the City award a contract to Andrew Davis (aka AJ Davis) of
  Project Street Gold, to design, construct, and install the outdoor public art piece
  in the Zinnia Courtyard.

  Staff recommends City Council approve the Contract Services Agreement with
  Andrew Davis of Project Street Gold to design, construct, and install the final
  outdoor public art in the Zinnia Courtyard in the amount not-to-exceed $80,000.
  The estimated completion date for this project is April 2024.
  Recommendation:

  Authorize the City Manager to execute the Contract Services Agreement with
  Andrew Davis of Project Street Gold for the design, construction, and installation
  of the outdoor public art piece in the Signal Hill Public Library Zinnia Courtyard,
  in an amount not to exceed $80,000, in a form approved by the City Attorney.
  d.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT REGISTER DATED DECEMBER 12, 2023

  Summary:

  The Contract Amendment Register is a listing of proposed contract amendments
  and project change orders eligible for streamlined processing based upon the
  following criteria as documented in the City’s Purchasing Policy:

  ·  Funds have been authorized as part of the adopted fiscal year Operating
  Budget
  ·  Staff are satisfied with the goods/services received to date and
  ·  The City Manager reviewed and approved each amendment for
  streamlined processing.

  The contract amendment being presented for City Council consideration is as
  follows:

  Michael Baker International, Inc. for on-call water engineering services.
  Amendment No. 7 extends the term through June 30, 2024.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.

  Page 7 of 10
 City Council  Regular  December 12, 2023

  Recommendation:

  Authorize the Contract Amendment Register dated December 12, 2023.
  e.  RESOLUTION AMENDING THE HOURLY PART-TIME SALARY SCHEDULE
  TO COMPLY WITH THE CALIFORNIA STATE MINIMUM WAGE LAW

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider an adjustment to the part-time salary schedule
  that would update the City’s hourly, part-time salary ranges to comply with the
  California State minimum wage law. The State’s hourly minimum wage will
  increase effective January 1, 2024, to $16.00 an hour. The City has five existing
  part-time classifications (Intern, Library Aide, Maintenance Helper, Police Aide,
  and Recreation Leader) whose wages would need to be updated accordingly to
  comply with the law. City Council approval of the proposed Resolution is
  required to update the salary schedule effective January 1, 2024.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendation:

  Adopt a resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING SALARY RANGES FOR HOURLY, PART-TIME
  EMPLOYEES PREVIOUSLY ADOPTED BY RESOLUTION NO. 2023-06-6748
  TO COMPLY WITH THE CALIFORNIA MINIMUM WAGE LAW AND
  REPEALING ALL PRIOR RESOLUTIONS
  f.  FEE WAIVER REQUEST FOR THE FRIENDS OF SIGNAL HILL LIBRARY
  (FOSHL)

  Summary:

  Staff received a request from the FOSHL, a Signal Hill non-profit, for a facility
  and staffing fee waiver for the use of the Signal Hill Public Library Learning
  Center for the following Tuesday dates in 2024: January 9, March 12, May 14,
  July 9, September 10, and November 12 from 4:45 p.m. to 6:45 p.m. along with
  Thursday, May 16 and Thursday, October 17, 2024, from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00
  p.m. Additionally, FOSHL is requesting permission to promote its fundraising
  events by displaying banners on the Signal Hill Point Terrace and at Hill Street
  and Temple Avenue.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Page 8 of 10
 City Council  Regular  December 12, 2023

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that City Council review and approve FOSHL’s fee waiver
  request for use of the Signal Hill Library Community Room, costs for City staff
  and supplies, and approve FOSHL to display its banners for book sale
  promotion events.
  g.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS AND MONTHLY TRANSACTION REPORT

  Summary:

  The Schedule of Investments is a listing of all surplus funds invested for both the
  City and the Successor Agency to the former Signal Hill Redevelopment Agency
  as of the date shown on the report. The monthly transaction report provides the
  changes in investments for the prior month.

  Strategic Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.
  Recommendation:

  Receive and file.
  h.  WARRANT REGISTER DATED DECEMBER 12, 2023

  Summary:

  The Warrant Register is a listing of all general disbursements issued since the
  prior warrant register and warrants to be released upon City Council approval.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.
  Recommendation:

  Authorize payment of the Warrant Register dated December 12, 2023.
  i.  APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES

  Summary:

  Regular Meeting of November 24, 2023.
  Recommendation:

  Page 9 of 10
 City Council  Regular  December 12, 2023

  Approve the meeting minutes.
(8)  COUNCIL AGENDA--NEW BUSINESS

  COUNCIL MEMBER WILSON
  COUNCIL MEMBER JONES
  COUNCIL MEMBER COPELAND
  VICE MAYOR WOODS
  MAYOR HANSEN
(9)  ADJOURNMENT

  Tonight’s meeting will be adjourned to the next regular meeting of the Signal Hill City
  Council to be held on Tuesday, January 9, 2024, at 6:00 p.m., in the Council Chamber
  of City Hall, 2175 Cherry Avenue, Signal Hill, CA 90755. There will be no regular Signal
  Hill City Council meeting on Tuesday, December 26, 2023.
CITIZEN PARTICIPATION

  Routine matters are handled most quickly and efficiently if contact is made with the City
  department directly concerned. However, if you would like to request that a matter be
  presented for City Council consideration, you may do so by writing to the City Council,
  City Clerk, or City Manager. The deadline for agenda items is 12 noon on the Tuesday
  preceding the Council and Agency meetings. The complete agenda, including back up
  materials is available on the City website on the Friday preceding the meeting.

  If you need special assistance beyond what is normally provided to participate in City
  meetings, the City will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner.
  Please call the City Clerk's office at (562) 989-7305 at least 48 hours prior to the
  meeting to inform us of your particular needs and to determine if accommodation is
  feasible.
